script: "She hid a $300 scam—now she's begging for $100. My heart shattered.". I walked in the door and she was already swiping that app on her phone like it was a new Snapchat filter. She told me she'd dropped $300 TTD into it, and that she kept it a secret because she knew I'd be like, "No way, that's a scam." (I didn't even bother to ask what the app was, honestly.) Fast forward to tonight—she's glued to her phone for hours, typing away like she's coding a space‑rocket. I catch a flash of the same app on her screen. A text pops up: "Pay $100 USD to unlock your funds." My brain flips to panic mode. I slam the question on her: "What's that about?" She blurts out, "I got $5,500, trying to move it to my account." I know it's a scam—there's no way that's legit. I am mad, not at the money she lost, but at her letting that scam slip past her. I should've stopped her when she first brought it up. The audacity, right? (I know, right?)
